paper.title: Learning the Optimal Path and DNN Partition for Collaborative Edge Inference

settings.name_in_paper: Adversarial group linear bandits (AGLB) with switching cost
unmapped: G groups, each with its own unknown linear parameter theta_g; learner picks a group and an arm within the group
Adversary picks a binary attack vector over groups each round; reward of an attacked group is exactly 0 (attack is observable through the 0 reward)
Hybrid stochastic (within-group linear) / adversarial (across-group) reward generation
Switching cost tau per group switch, known to the learner
Benchmark: best fixed group in hindsight, playing the per-round optimal arm within that group
settings.definition_quote: the learner receives a reward r^t(g^t, x^t, a^t) = a^t(g^t)\cdot (\mu(g^t, x^t) + \epsilon^t) ... if the group g^{t} \neq g^{t-1}, then the learner also suffers an extra penalty of \tau ... The total regret is the sum of the reward regret and switching regret

tuning: block lengths B_n = max{ceil(n^a),1} with a = 1

source.quote: For any $\delta \in (0, 1)$, by choosing $\beta = T^{-1/4}\sqrt{\log(T)}$, $\eta = T^{-3/4}$, $B_n = \max\{\lceil n^a \rceil, 1\}$ and $a = 1$, EXPUCB yields, with probability at least $1-\delta$, the following expected regret bound $R_T \le O(T^{1/2}), S_T \le O(T^{3/4}\sqrt{\log(T)})$, $\reg(T) = O(T^{3/4}\sqrt{\log(T)})$.

results.notes: Total regret = expected reward regret + switching cost. Statement mixes 'with probability 1-delta' and 'expected regret', so quantity left unspecified though probability marked high_probability. Comparator is the best fixed group (with per-round optimal arm in that group). Dependence on G, d, tau, sigma hidden. Conclusion states O(T^{3/4} log T).

source.quote: EXPUCB yields, with probability at least $1-\delta$, the following expected regret bound $R_T \le O(T^{1/2}), S_T \le O(T^{3/4}\sqrt{\log(T)})$

results.notes: Reward regret only (excluding switching cost). The proof instead concludes R_T = O(T^{3/4} sqrt(log T)) and S_T = O(T^{1/2}); the statement appears to swap the two. Recorded as stated.
Bound on cumulative switching cost S_T (paper's S_T, not number of environment switches). The proof gives S_T <= tau(Gamma+1) = O(T^{1/2}), which contradicts the statement; recorded as stated.
